chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: The filter method creates an array filled with all array elements of another array that

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: pass a test, provided as a function.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: Filter does not execute the function for array elements without values, and it does not change

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: the original array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: Here's the basic syntax of the filter method.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: First we create a new variable to hold the new array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: Then we refer to the array that we want to filter using .filter.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: The filter method accepts a function callback, and that function has access to the current

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: element, index, and the entire original array.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: In this example we have some numbers.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: If our goal is to filter only the even numbers, we can set it up like this.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: Here we are only interested in the value.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: Then we are returning the value only if it is divisible by 2 with no remainder.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: In our new variable we now have an array with only the even numbers.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: We can shorten this by using an arrow function.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: We can also shorten the variable from value to n since that would make sense.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: And instead of checking if it is equal to 0, we can instead check for false, since 0

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: would be equal to false and that is what we are looking for.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: A more common use case would be filtering objects.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: In this example we have an array of objects containing all of the Star Wars movies.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: If we had a movie app or website, we would want to provide a way for our users to filter

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: the items.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: So if we only want the most recent movies, we can filter it this way.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: For the variable we will call it L for element.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: Then we get the year and check to see if it is greater than or equal to 2015.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
chunks.text: Now we get only the 3 most recent Star Wars movies.

chunks.title: JavaScript Array Filter Method In 90 Seconds
